lots.guide_summary: All AUD hammer, no conversion (rate 1.00). 2 close SOLD: Coogan's single-door cabinets at Gowans, $190 (blackwood bedside with the same label, 16 Jan 2026) and $210 (oak cabinet, 6 Mar 2026). Category guides, all SOLD: unlabelled single-door bedsides and pot cupboards in Armitage's own room $15 to $170 (Jul to Sep 2026) and at Gowans $50 to $150 (Jan to Sep 2026); Coogan's case furniture at Armitage $70 (dressing chest) and $250 (glazed bookcase). Coogan's tables, hallstands and a tray made $40 to $150 (dropped as different forms), so the label brings a modest premium at best. No UNSOLD or ASKING evidence found.
lots.working: Same-item SOLD (close: same maker and same single-door bedside form, both within 24 months): $190 (Gowans 382880, 16 Jan 2026) and $210 (Gowans 393874, 6 Mar 2026). Keep: lowest $190 / 1.22 = $155.74, rounded down to $155 hammer ($189.10 all-in). Flip: likely resale about $150 hammer, set between Armitage's own results for good single-door bedsides ($95 to $170) and the Gowans Coogan's results ($190 to $210), because Coogan's pieces at Armitage have shown little label premium ($70 dressing chest); less an assumed 15% vendor commission ($22.50) and $0 outbound postage (resold through a local auction, buyer collects) = $127.50; / 2.44 = $52.25, rounded down to $50. Inbound freight $0 (pickup at 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay). Both Coogan's comparables are more decorative Edwardian designs than this plain Arts and Crafts piece, and the candidate may be refinished, so treat $155 as a ceiling, not a target.
lots.confidence_reason: COOGAN'S TASMANIA label read in photo 2, two close same-maker SOLD results opened at Gowans, and six Armitage own-room results opened. Not High because the two Coogan's sales are different designs, the finish may be a refinish, and the interior and back panel are not shown.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped as different forms (prices, dates and bids all matched the Gowans API): 377431 pair of retro myrtle bedsides $150 for the pair (28 Nov 2025; a pair, mid-century drawer-over-door style); 405333 leadlight blackwood display cabinet $190 (1 May 2026; display cabinet); and the Coogan's brand-context items 390527 two-tier side table $80 (20 Feb 2026), 387488 hallstand $140 (6 Feb 2026), 429527 entrance table $115 (14 Aug 2026), 442809 side table $40 (9 Oct 2026), plus those named in the notes: 370366 plant stand $102 (31 Oct 2025), 399569 occasional table $65 (27 Mar 2026), 427903 side table $60 (7 Aug 2026) and 384589 hallstand $150 (sold 23 Jan 2026, not 22 Jan as written). Also left out from my own Armitage search: 3045818 Coogan's blackwood serving tray with label $60 (9 Sep 2026) and 2947227 two blackwood bedside chests of drawers, one damaged, $45 (17 Jun 2026), both different forms. Added: 6 Armitage own-room results found by reading all 30 closed Armitage catalogue pages (17 Jun to 30 Sep 2026; 10,482 of 11,234 lots with bids carry the on-the-market badge) and opening the past lot pages. WebSearch was capped this turn, so no site search was possible. The researcher's Gowans figures for the kept entries all match.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2, enlarged: printed paper label COOGAN'S TASMANIA. with fields Job No., Order No., Design No., Bench No., Dept. and Fxd. by; handwriting reads Order No. 900 or 1900, Design No. 17 (probable), Bench No. 104, Dept. 3 and initials after Fxd. by (illegible); Job No. blank or illegible. Water stained, on rough weathered timber, the same printed form as the label on Gowans lot 382880. Photo 1: single door of two flat panels with a centre stile, brass oval flush catch, brass butt hinges, square tapered legs, shaped bracket under the front rail, flat side panel. The top is three boards in different tones (dark, pale, dark), which may be blackwood heart and sapwood or a later replacement rather than deliberate banding. Glossy finish suggests a refinish.
lots.condition: Front, side and top look clean and glossy, probably refinished; no splits, chips or lifted joints visible. Interior, shelf, back panel and underside not shown; the back carrying the label is weathered and water stained.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is the finish original or refinished, and is the top original to the cabinet (its boards are different colours)? Please confirm the COOGAN'S label photo is from this cabinet, the timber (blackwood?), the size (H-76 L-61 D-44 cm), whether there is a shelf inside, and any splits, repairs or a replaced back panel.

lots.guide_summary: All AUD hammer, no conversion (rate 1.00). 2 close SOLD at Gowans: $15 (small box drinks cabinet with decanters and glasses, 14 Aug 2026) and $140 (mid-century fall-front drinks cabinet on legs, 23 Jan 2026), both on only 2 bids. 3 category-guide SOLD at Gowans: $40 (Art Deco drinks cabinet), $110 (teak wall cocktail cabinet plus a display cabinet) and $150 (G-Plan drinks cabinet). No drinks or cocktail cabinet sold in any of Armitage's 30 closed catalogues (17 Jun to 30 Sep 2026). No verified UNSOLD or ASKING evidence: Invaluable hides sold prices behind a login, and the dealer listings were trolleys or large named bar cabinets.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD: the cabinet is unbranded and no sale of a small fitted portable drinks cabinet of this type and era was found. The two close Gowans results ($15 and $140) differ in style or size, so they are guides only and no maximum bid is set (keep 0, flip 0). As a guide only, Tasmanian drinks cabinets of various kinds made $15 to $150 hammer in the last year ($18 to $183 all-in at Armitage's 22%).
lots.confidence_reason: No maker or mark, no same-item SOLD, the close comparables differ in style or size, and no mainland price could be verified (Invaluable login wall).
lots.dropped_entries: Gowans: 431889 Art Deco cocktail cabinet $20 (21 Aug 2026) dropped, a large burr-walnut sideboard with a display top, not comparable; 382120 reproduction three-door drinks cabinet $3 (12 Dec 2025, 0 bids, glass missing) dropped as a damaged reproduction. Both figures matched the API. Armitage: the four catalogue-page entries are real (LP album cabinet $405 on 17 Jun 2026, oak two-drawer cabinet $100 on 9 Sep 2026, Tasmanian oak library trolley $310 on 29 Jul 2026, teak sideboard $70 on 30 Sep 2026; all confirmed on the closed catalogue pages with the on-the-market badge) but none is a drinks cabinet, so dropped. Invaluable: all 23 entries dropped (14 SOLD, 8 UNSOLD, 1 ASKING). curl gets an AWS WAF challenge (HTTP 202); WebFetch loaded 13 pages and every SOLD page shows 'Sold: Log in to view', so no price, last bid or bid count could be seen. Loaded pages confirmed lot, house, date and estimate: 1539 Lawsons 10 Apr 2025 est 80-120 sold; 1097 Lawsons 20 Mar 2025 est 300-400 Passed (last bid not shown); 1725 Barsby 17 Aug 2025 est 350-500 sold (110 x 125 x 34 cm); 1081 Leonard Joel 17 Jul 2025 est 400-600 sold (73 x 88 x 50 cm); 1024 Leonard Joel 1 Aug 2024 and 1041 Lawsons 18 Jul 2024 (both over 24 months); lot 79 David G Smith 9 Nov 2024; 1572 Lawsons 8 May 2025; 1448 Lawsons 10 Sep 2026; 1179 Leonard Joel 15 Oct 2026; 67 Yarra Valley 5 Mar 2026; 1206 Leonard Joel 5 Mar 2026; 5085 Bargain Hunt 2 Dec 2024. Pages that returned empty: 462, 1332, 1201, 757, 1743, 1606, 255, 1268, 1251 and the live lot 1057. Most were larger, design-led, fold-out vinyl or Chinese bar pieces anyway. Dealers: prices confirmed from each shop's product record, all in stock (Vintage Upcycle $295 three-tier trolley and $595 Rodd and Philipp drinks cart; Retro Bay $1,190 Chiswell sideboard bar and $2,490 Burgess bar cabinet), but none is a small portable drinks cabinet, so dropped.
lots.key_photo_findings: Four photos: box-form cabinet on four brass ball castors, chrome side handles, barrel lock with a chrome star escutcheon and a key on a tag, lift-up lid and fall front on chrome stays both lined in orange woodgrain laminate, fitted timber rack with about 20 round holes and about 12 square compartments, bare timber interior. No maker label, stamp or retailer plate visible on the lock, hinges, stays or inside; tags are handwritten auction tags. Golden-brown veneer with rounded front corners, 1950s to 60s style.
lots.condition: Veneer and laminate look sound with light wear on the lid edges and minor marks; some staining on the interior floor; lock and castors not shown working. No glasses or decanters included.
lots.question_for_armitage: Does the lock work and is the key included? Is there any maker's or retailer's label inside the lid, on the fall front or underneath? Do all four castors turn, and are the laminate and veneer edges free of lifting or chips?

lots.guide_summary: All AUD hammer, no conversion (rate 1.00). 8 close SOLD: Armitage's own room $25, $80 and $125 (Jul to Sep 2026) and Gowans $35 to $130 (Feb to Aug 2026). The three with about the same Carlton content as lot 563 (5 to 7 floral leaf pieces) made $35 (Gowans 416349), $50 (Gowans 408739) and $80 (Armitage lot 452, which also had uranium glass and decanters); larger all-Carlton groups made $90 to $130. Category guides, all SOLD: mixed china with a Carlton share $3 to $90; generic two-box china lots $25 to $100. Four Gowans lots naming Carlton passed in (420091 and its re-offer 421718, 422742 and its re-offer 424364) with no bid amount shown, so they are noted but not listed. No ASKING evidence found.
lots.working: Same-item set = lots with about the same Carlton content as lot 563 (5 to 7 floral leaf pieces) sold in the last 24 months: $35 (Gowans 416349, 19 Jun 2026), $50 (Gowans 408739, 15 May 2026) and $80 (Armitage lot 452, 9 Sep 2026). Keep: lowest $35 / 1.22 = $28.69, rounded down to $25 hammer ($30.50 all-in). Flip: likely resale about $50 hammer (median of the three), less an assumed 15% vendor commission ($7.50) and $0 outbound postage (resold through a local auction, buyer collects) = $42.50; / 2.44 = $17.42, rounded down to $15. Inbound freight $0 (pickup at 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay). The filler porcelain adds little. A flip has almost no margin, so this is a small keep buy only.
lots.confidence_reason: The moulded pattern clearly matches Carlton Ware Australian Design Apple Blossom-type ware (the same pieces appear in Armitage lot 452 and in Gowans lots with backstamps), and three same-content SOLD results were opened, one in Armitage's own room. Not High because no backstamp is visible in the single photo and condition cannot be checked.
